description: Ganoderma lucidum, known as Reishi or Lingzhi, is a woody, shelf-like polypore famous for its glossy, varnished reddish-brown cap and prized in East Asian traditional medicine. It is too tough and woody to eat as food but is used as a medicinal decoction, tea, or extract. The name 'G. lucidum' has long been applied broadly, but molecular work shows it is a species complex; G. lucidum sensu stricto is European/temperate, while much non-Asian and cultivated material represents distinct species (e.g. G. lingzhi/G. sichuanense for the cultivated Asian taxon, G. curtisii and G. sessile in North America).
edibilityNotes: Not edible as a food: the fruiting body is woody, corky, and indigestible. It is non-poisonous and is used medicinally as a decoction (tea), tincture, or powdered extract rather than eaten whole. Not a culinary mushroom; medicinal claims are not evaluated here.
habitat: at the base of hardwood trees and stumps
distribution: Cosmopolitan as traditionally circumscribed, though true G. lucidum sensu stricto is European/temperate; many regional records represent distinct species within the G. lucidum complex.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Ganoderma tsugae
dangerousLookalikes.note: Hemlock varnish shelf; nearly identical glossy varnished red-brown crust. Distinguished primarily by host (grows on conifers, especially hemlock/Tsuga) versus G. lucidum on hardwoods, and reliably only by genetics. Not toxic, but the most easily confused look-alike.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Ganoderma curtisii
dangerousLookalikes.note: North American varnished polypore long misidentified as G. lucidum; distinguished by genetics and often a more elongated stipe and paler tones. Not dangerous, but a taxonomic look-alike.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Ganoderma sichuanense
dangerousLookalikes.note: Linked to the cultivated Asian 'Lingzhi' (often treated as G. lingzhi); molecularly distinct from European G. lucidum. Visually very similar.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Ganoderma applanatum
dangerousLookalikes.note: Artist's conk; lacks the glossy varnished crust and is perennial with a flat dull grey-brown upper surface and a white pore surface that bruises brown.
